props.gloss_en: Rav Huna: one who shakes his cloak on Shabbat is liable to a sin-offering
we said this only of new [garments]; of old ones we have no problem
we said this only of black [garments]; of white and red ones we have no problem
and that is where he is particular about them
Ulla, seeing the Rabbis of Pumbedita shake their cloaks: the Rabbis are desecrating Shabbat
Rav Yehuda to them: shake [them] in his face
Rav Yehuda: we are not particular about anything
Rav Yosef, to Abaye who hesitated to hand him his hat because there was dew on it: shake [it] and throw [it]
Rav Yosef: we are not particular about anything
R' Yochanan: one who goes out on Shabbat with a folded cloak lying on his shoulder is liable to a sin-offering
the baraita: cloth merchants who go out on Shabbat with folded cloaks lying on their shoulders are liable to a sin-offering
the baraita: they said it not of cloth merchants alone but of every person -- only that sellers usually go out so
the baraita: a shopkeeper who goes out with coins bound in his sheet is liable to a sin-offering -- and not a shopkeeper alone but every person
the baraita: runners may go out with scarves on their shoulders -- and not runners alone but every person
R' Yehuda: Hyrcanus son of R' Eliezer ben Hyrcanus went out on Shabbat with a scarf on his shoulder, but with a thread wound on his finger
when the matter came before the Sages they said: even if no thread is wound on his finger
Rav Chisda: the halakha is [so] even though no thread is wound on his fingers
R' Elai: it is forbidden to make a marzev on Shabbat
R' Zeira: the marzev is Babylonian pockets
R' Zeira, of the first [fold] R' Yirmeya showed him: forbidden
R' Zeira, of the second [fold]: forbidden
Rav Pappa: hold this rule -- whatever is [done] with intent to gather up is forbidden
Rav Pappa: whatever is for adornment is permitted
Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi would adorn himself with his sheet
once Rebbi went out to the field with both sides of his cloak lying on his shoulder
did not R' Meir hold one liable to a sin-offering in this?
Rebbi: was R' Meir exacting to this extent?
Rebbi let down his cloak
Rav Dimi: the one who spoke before Rebbi was Yehoshua ben Zeiruz, son of R' Meir's father-in-law
Ravin: it was not Yehoshua ben Zeiruz but Yehoshua ben Kefusai, R' Akiva's son-in-law
did not R' Akiva hold one liable to a sin-offering in this?
Rebbi: was R' Akiva exacting to this extent?
Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yehuda: 'was asked' is what was stated
